title: WinBack
subtitle: Omega Force · Nintendo 64

body: WinBack is Omega Force's Nintendo 64 third-person shooter about Jean-Luc Cougar infiltrating a facility seized by terrorists. Their control of a laser satellite gives the mission a larger threat, but progress depends on surviving the immediate arrangement of corridors, guards and firing positions. Jean-Luc can take cover at corners and emerge to aim, making the environment part of his defence. The player repeatedly judges where it is safe to stand before committing to a shot that briefly exposes him to the opposing fire.

Aiming holds Jean-Luc in place while the stick directs a laser sight. Movement and firing therefore become distinct decisions, with a useful position established before the next target is engaged. Ammunition, weapons and opportunities to crouch or roll give the player additional responses to an ambush. Navigation also introduces keys and laser traps, making observation useful beyond combat. The next obstacle may ask for a shot at a control box rather than another enemy, connecting the same aiming system to progress through the facility.

Released in 1999, WinBack gave console players an early example of building a third-person firefight around cover, exposure and a visible aiming line. Its PlayStation 2 adaptation followed in Japan in 2000, with revised presentation and multiplayer options. The original game later joined Nintendo's classic-game service. Its place in the genre's history comes from the clarity of that spatial relationship: an ordinary corner becomes a useful tactical object because it determines what the player can see, what can see them and when a shot can safely be attempted.
story_headings: An operation fought from one safe position to another
Stop moving to line up the shot
A cover system before the later standard
